title: Home-Site Lease Clause: One Open Lease per Customer
content:
**Clause — one home-site lease at a time**

1. A home site under the Home-Site Lease is leased to the household that lives in the home on it, and a customer may hold only one home-site lease across all Hearthstone communities at a time (a limit of 1 per customer).
2. A residency application is taken only when the applicant holds no other lease in applied, approved, active or in-default status. The applicant's other leases are read from the company's lease records for that customer, not from the applicant's own account of them.
3. A lease in notice-to-vacate status does not count against the limit, so a resident relocating between sites may apply for the new site while the notice on the old one runs.
4. A lease that is closed or denied never counts.
5. An application that would breach the limit is not taken; the caller is told which lease already counts.

### Status of the customer's other lease

| Status of the other lease on record | Counts against the limit | New application |
|---|---|---|
| applied | yes | not taken |
| approved | yes | not taken |
| active | yes | not taken |
| in default | yes | not taken |
| notice to vacate | no | may be taken |
| closed | no | may be taken |
| denied | no | may be taken |

### Hypothetical cases

- A resident of Saguaro Vista whose lease is in notice-to-vacate status applies for a site at Willow Bend Estates: the Saguaro Vista lease does not count, so the application may be taken.
- A customer whose earlier application at Cedar Hollow is still applied (undecided) asks to apply at Conestoga Meadows: the pending application counts, so the new one is not taken and the caller is told that the Cedar Hollow application is the lease that counts.
